name: Taylor Swift
summary: A pop musician who avoided politics early in her career and has been openly political since 2018. She has endorsed Democratic candidates, describes herself as pro-choice, and has advocated for LGBTQ rights, against systemic racism and for gun control, mostly through social media posts and endorsements rather than detailed policy positions.

abortion-legal.rationale: She described herself as 'obviously' pro-choice (2019), said she was 'terrified' when Roe v. Wade was overturned (2022), and in 2024 praised a candidate for defending 'a woman's right to her own body'.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: She called systemic racism toward people of color 'terrifying' and 'sickening', urged removal of Tennessee monuments to racist figures, backed making Juneteenth a national holiday and donated to the NAACP Legal Defense Fund. No stated view on specific remedial policies such as reparations.

limit-guns.rationale: She has publicly supported gun control and donated to March for Our Lives, without endorsing strict limits on ownership specifically.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: She objected publicly to a Senate candidate's opposition to same-sex marriage and to businesses refusing service to gay couples, said discrimination based on sexual orientation is wrong, and campaigned for the Equality Act.

notes: Born 13 December 1989; living as of the audit. Her public political record is a set of endorsements and social-issue statements (abortion, LGBTQ rights, racism, gun control, voter registration); she has stated no positions on economic policy, foreign policy, or most structural questions in this test, so those are null rather than inferred from her Democratic endorsements.
